To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we cloned a new member of the G-protein coupled receptors family that is most closely related to the neuropeptide Y receptor Y2.
a novel gene product, homologous to the neuropeptide Y receptor family was identified.

we cloned a novel member of the seven transmembran-spanning receptor superfamily with highest amino acid identity to the neuropeptide Y receptor subtype Y2, that we determined its gene structure and localisation, that we analysed its mRNA expression in human tissues and in rat brain, and that we characterised its protein expression in cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning and characterisation (expression analysis, localisation, function) of the human and mouse GPR74 genes and their products.
the identification of a novel G-proteincoupled receptor, which is closely related to the neuropeptide Y (NPY) receptor family and which may be a new member of this receptor family.
the molecular cloning and characterisation, the localisation and expression pattern of the GPR74 gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GPR74 is a novel G-proteincoupled receptor with a unique structure, a distinct tissue expression pattern and an unknown function.
GPR74 is the closest relative to the Y-receptors and is a member of the Y-like family.
the GPR74 gene product is a novel G-proteincoupled receptor with homology to neuropeptide Y receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GPR74 is a novel member of the G-protein-coupled receptor superfamily and is the closest relative of the Y-receptors, which are known to be expressed in brain and heart.
we have cloned a new GPCR, which has homologies to the NPY-receptor family, but does not seem to be a NPY-receptor itself.
GPR74 is a novel GPCR with homology to neuropeptide Y (NPY)-like receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we cloned and characterised a novel gene product, a G-protein coupled seven transmembrane receptor, GPR74.
GPR74 is the first member of a novel G-proteincoupled receptor family.
GPR74 is a novel gene product with homology to a seven transmembrane domain receptor superfamily, which is most closely related to the NPY receptor family.
